items.title: Sarah Shafiq, Coalition of Muslim Women
notes: S. Shafiq appeared before Council to speak to the National Day of Remembrance and Action Against Islamophobia in order to commemorate the Quebec City Mosque Attack. She remembered the individuals that were killed in the attack and the need to work tirelessly to combat hate. S. Shafiq called for polices that support marginalized communities so that no one needs to leave in fear.

attachments.name: 8.1 - Sarah Shafiq, Coalition of Muslim Women Presentation.pdf

items.title: Uzma Bhutto, Coalition of Muslim Women
notes:
U. Bhutto provided a presentation outlining the anti hate services work that the Coalition of Muslim Women has been undertaking. She provided an overview of the support they have been providing to victims, and the outreach and education work with communities regarding the importance of recognizing and reporting hate. She requested that the Region provide ongoing program support, noting that without financial support there will be fewer instances of hate reported and a weakened response as a result.

Responding to questions S. Shafiq and U. Bhutto explained that the Coalition of Muslim Women received initial funding from the province. They noted that the anti hate service has been supported by the Region. S. Shafiq noted that the full time coordinator has been reduced to part time and that $120,000 is needed for a year.

items.title: Administration and Finance Committee Summary - January 14, 2025
Board of Health Update
notes:
Dr. H. Wang provided an update on the winter illness season, noting the Public Health continues to monitor outbreaks in long term care and congregate living settings, which are consistent with other areas. She noted that there are no local cases of measles but highlighted that the Chief Public Health Officer of Canada has issued a statement that Canada is seeing an increase in measles and the majority of cases in Canada are with individuals that are unvaccinated including children under the age of one, who are not eligible for the vaccination. 

Received for information.

notes:
William Short, Regional Clerk, introduced the report noting that the Council needs to declare the seat vacant and staff will bring back a report back outlining the options for Council to fill the vacancy.

B. Vrbanovic brought forward an amendment to change the date of the Special Council meeting to March 4, 2025 to allow for the results of the provincial election to be known before Council makes a decision on the vacancy.

motions.item_title: Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee Summary - January 14, 2025
motions.text: That the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee recommends as follows That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the commencement of the process to transfer Speedsville Road between Maple Grove Road (Regional Road 38) and Eagle Street (Regional Road 39) from the City of Cambridge to the Regional Municipality of Waterloo as described in report TSD-TRP-25-001, dated January 14, 2025: Provide notice to the public of the proposed transfer of the above road segment from the City of Cambridge in accordance with the Region’s Notice Policy; Commence the process to amend the Road Consolidation By-Law 01-059 (Regional Road System) to assume the above noted road segment from the City of Cambridge, effective upon passing of the by-law; and Commence the process to amend Traffic and Parking By-law 16-023 to reflect the addition of existing traffic regulations on the section of road to be assumed by the Region of Waterloo.
motions.text_html:
That the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee recommends as follows

  1. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the commencement of the process to transfer Speedsville Road between Maple Grove Road (Regional Road 38) and Eagle Street (Regional Road 39) from the City of Cambridge to the Regional Municipality of Waterloo as described in report TSD-TRP-25-001, dated January 14, 2025:
    1. Provide notice to the public of the proposed transfer of the above road segment from the City of Cambridge in accordance with the Region’s Notice Policy;
    2. Commence the process to amend the Road Consolidation By-Law 01-059 (Regional Road System) to assume the above noted road segment from the City of Cambridge, effective upon passing of the by-law; and
    3. Commence the process to amend Traffic and Parking By-law 16-023 to reflect the addition of existing traffic regulations on the section of road to be assumed by the Region of Waterloo.

Part-time professor at Durham College teaching Alternative Dispute Resolution to Law Clerk students. Member of the Law Society of Ontario
